principle:
## Depth: every noun opens where it stands

Every name, figure and word the game prints is a thing in the world, and a thing in the world can be looked at more closely. The name is the control: you press "Stress", or "Reykjavík", or "Everyday Checking", and it opens. There is no Open button, no Details button, no chevron and no tooltip, because a thing does not need a handle to be looked at.

What a thing opens into is declared once, for the kind of thing it is, in `src/ui/looks/`. A screen never writes what is inside a thing; a screen only says which thing it is naming. So the same calendar entry opens the same way on Home and on the Calendar, and it opens the same way from a notification that is about it, because openability belongs to the entry and not to the screen it happens to be printed on.

A look leads with a sentence, in the second person, true right now. Then, if there is more, the facts. Then the ways further in, each of which says what is behind it before you take it. A look never opens into arithmetic: where a figure is SLATE's calibration, one footnote line at the bottom says so, in the world's words, and that is the whole of it. The floor of every chain is a person, a place, a thing or a moment. A look that would bottom out in a formula, a field name or a record has gone wrong, and the look is wrong, not the world.

A thing that cannot be looked at is not painted as though it can. A look that resolves to nothing says what became of it, in a sentence, in its own voice.
rules: 1. A screen names a subject; it never writes a body. Depth lives in `src/ui/looks/<kind>.tsx` behind `defineLook`, one declaration per kind, and nowhere else. A `useState` holding drill state in a screen is a bug.

2. The noun is the control. A look is opened by pressing the world's own word for the thing — `button.link`, which app.css:328 already defines and already calls "a name that is also a way in". No control anywhere in the system is labelled Open, Show, Hide, Details, More, View or Expand.

3. A look is painted only when it resolves. `<Open>` asks `lookExists` first and renders its children as plain text when the subject is not there. An unregistered kind throws in development and renders as plain text in production. Nothing ever opens onto a toast, and nothing ever opens onto Under Construction.

4. Every view states `name`, `kind`, `summary` and `gone`, and all four are required. `summary` is one sentence, second person, present tense, true at this instant. `gone` is one sentence in the world's voice for when the subject is no longer there.

5. `name` is the world's word for the thing and is the only string the trail prints. `kind` is the type word, it renders as an eyebrow above the name, and it never enters the name. No `name` or `kind` contains an underscore, a slash, a run of four or more digits, or the text of any registered kind.
6. Prose first, facts second, ways third. A body may hold at most one grid of `Stat`s, and only below its opening sentence. A body that is only a grid of `Stat`s is a record view and is rejected.
7. Every way in carries a `detail` line saying what is behind it. The graph is readable without walking it.

8. Facets are tabs, not levels. A tab is another face of the same thing; a look is a different thing. Facets are a typed field on the view and render as `.tabs`/`.tab` (app.css:749-762). A facet is never addressable as a subject.
9. Narrowing a set is a filter inside the level you are in, never a new level. Choosing among 813 attributes uses the picker shape in place. A new level means a different object.

10. No formula is ever a level. Coefficients may appear inside a sentence; they may not be the sentence. `provenance` is one line at the foot of a body and is not itself openable. Any look that answers "why" builds its factors with `buildFactors` and renders them through `redactForPlayer` (core/audit.ts:138), and never grows a second explanation.

11. The container is computed, not chosen. A view declares its `parent` subject. Opening a child of what you are already reading expands it in place; crossing to a different object opens the look pane; a subject marked `dwell` opens full width at `/look`. Below 900px every look expands in place, because `.grid-2`, `.grid-3` and `.grid-4` are already one column there (app.css:948).
12. A modal commits; a look only reads. Sleep, Skip To Event and Delete Save stay modals because they ask a question and change the world. Nothing read-only opens a modal again.

13. `title=` is not depth. No `title` attribute in `src/ui` carries information that is not also on the screen. `Term` and `Meter.hint` are deleted, and `.cal-event { cursor: pointer }` is deleted with them.

14. Depth is session state. The open path lives in `GameProvider` and in `sessionStorage`, and the leaf subject rides in `?look=` on the route so a look can be linked to and opened by a tool. Nothing about looking is written into the save.
mechanism:
**The spine is a registry whose views return data, not markup.** `defineLook(kind, view)` declares, once per kind of thing, how to find it in the live world and what a person sees when they look at it. `view.look()` returns a `Looked` — `{ name, kind, summary, parent, body?, facets?, ways?, acts?, provenance? }`. `body` is the only ReactNode in it. Everything that decides where a look sits, what it is called, and what it leads to is a plain value, which is why the whole drill graph can be crawled by a vitest test with no DOM. Designs that return JSX from `render` bury the graph's edges inside branches a test never reaches; this one cannot.

**A subject is `{ kind, id }`, never a captured object, and `id` is opaque to everything but the view.** So `at('city', 'is-39-reykjavik')`, `at('dial', 'person_000001/stress')` and `at('bracket', 'is/income/2')` are all first-class. That matters because SLATE's depth is not in its records — a fresh save is thirteen of those — it is in the anonymous sub-objects: `Wellbeing`, `Reputation`, `AttributeSheet`, `Posting`, `AuditFactor`, `Recurrence`, `TaxBracket`. A scheme that addresses only top-level ids misses almost all of the game.

It is also, deliberately, the exact shape the engine already emits and no screen has ever read: `refType`/`refId` on `CalendarEntry` (calendar.ts:57), `DecisionItem` (model.ts:784), `Notification` (model.ts:797), `ScheduledItem`, and every `LedgerTransaction` written by `sim.transfer`, `sim.income` and `sim.expense` (simulation.ts:503-589), plus `HistoryRecord.refs[]`. One function, `subjectForRef`, makes all of them openable at once, and a decision's Open button stops naming a room and starts naming its subject.

**Liveness by re-resolution.** A look holds an address. `LookHost` calls `resolveLook(sim, subject)` under `useWorld`, so it re-derives on every version bump — every world minute. This kills outright the bug that freezes `EntryDetail` today: `CalendarWorkspace.tsx:27` captures a `CalendarEntry`, which `toEntry` rebuilds on every read, while the clock runs a world minute per real second underneath it. If `resolve` comes back undefined the look stays on screen and prints its `gone` sentence with the trail still working, because a thing vanishing under you is worse than a thing that tells you it is gone.

**`parent` is the load-bearing field, and it does four jobs at once.** A view declares the subject it hangs beneath. From that one field:

- *The trail is materialised, not remembered.* Walk `parent` upward until it is undefined. A player who lands at depth 4 in one press — a meter on Home, a notification's ref, a restored `?look=` — arrives with `You › How You Are › Stress › Highly Strung` fully populated. A push-stack cannot do this; it would deposit them at depth 4 with one crumb, which is exactly the disorientation the feature is meant to remove.
- *The parent line comes free.* Above the name, dim: the parent's `name` and its `summary`. Layer 4 always shows layer 3's point, which is better context than a stacked pane's visible edge.
- *The container is computed.* If the subject you are opening declares the subject you are reading as its parent, it expands in place beneath the word you pressed. If it does not, you have crossed to a different object and the look pane opens. Nobody chooses; the relationship chooses. That is the one rule three separate reviews said would drift if it were left to authors.
- *The route stays short.* Because ancestry is derivable, `?look=` carries the leaf only: `/home?look=dial:person_000001/stress`. One helper, `screenRoute(route)`, strips it, and it is used at every existing place that compares a route — GameShell's `route === '/home'` and `startsWith('/workspace/')`, `WorkspaceRouter`'s `WORKSPACES[route]`, the rail's `aria-current`, and `navigate`'s crumb dedupe. A path-in-route scheme would have needed that helper at eight sites and a ninth would appear next month; a leaf-in-route scheme needs it once, at the boundary.

**Cycles fold instead of growing.** The subject graph is genuinely cyclic — Stress → what sheds it → Highly Strung → sleep quality → a dial. If `open()` is handed a subject already in the path, it pops to that index rather than pushing. The path is always a simple path; the graph is free to be a mesh.

**One view, three containers.** The same `Looked` renders in place (a `.look-body` stepping `--surface-2` then `--surface-3` and stopping — two steps, no more, because a fourth tint is invisible and a fourth indent is 64px of gutter on a phone), or in the look pane at 560px anchored right of `.main`, or full width at `/look` when the view sets `dwell` — the 813-attribute sheet, a year of daylight, a full statement. One authoring surface, three shapes, so a dense layer is never forked into a second implementation the gates measure separately.

**Escape and Modal, fixed on the way in.** `LookHost` registers one `keydown` on `window` at capture phase and calls `stopImmediatePropagation()`. That is the only mechanism that stops a single Escape from closing a look, the rail drawer (GameShell.tsx:38-43) and a `Modal` (primitives.tsx:126-130) at once, because all three currently listen on `window` at bubble. The same listener swallows bare `h` and `c` while a look is open — today they navigate the screen underneath an open dialog, since game-context.tsx:268-279 guards only INPUT, TEXTAREA and SELECT. And `Modal` gets portalled to the same layer host regardless: `.topbar` is `position: relative; z-index: 20` (app.css:587), it establishes a stacking context, and the three TimeControls dialogs inside it therefore render at 20 — beneath the mobile rail drawer at 30 and its shade at 29. There is no `createPortal` anywhere in `src/` today. Looks do not need that fix, which is precisely why nothing else will ever make it.

**Two primitives, one prop each, and roughly forty inert numbers become drillable in one edit.** `Stat` and `Meter` gain `look?: Subject`. Present, and the label renders as an `<Open>`; absent, and it renders as it does today. `Meter.hint` — the vestigial stub of exactly this feature — is deleted in the same pass, along with `Term`, so the tempting half-measures are gone.
layers:
The chain is Stress, and every number in it is already computed by `src/engine/systems/life.ts` and thrown away.

**Depth 1 — `person:person_000001`, in the pane.** Opened from the rail's "You" block, which is a plain `<div>` today (GameShell.tsx:141-149).

    Yourself
    Anna
    Holding up.
    [ How You Are · Standing · The Land · Money ]

Four facets, not four descents. `wellbeingSummary(person)` (life.ts:96-105) is the summary, live. The How You Are facet lists all **nine** dials as rows — energy, stress, sleep debt, morale, condition, fitness, travel fatigue, nourishment, hygiene. Six of those are simulated every day and appear on no screen in the game. This layer is exposure, not invention: it is `player.wellbeing`, rendered.

**Depth 2 — `dial:person_000001/stress`, in place.** Pressed from the Stress meter on Home, or from the row in the facet. Its `parent` is the person, so from the facet it expands where it stands; from Home it opens the pane with the trail already reading `You › How You Are › Stress`, because `trailTo` walked `parent` upward rather than replaying clicks.

    One Of Your Nine
    Stress
    Eighteen, and coming down. Nothing’s adding to it — that only
    starts when you’re running on empty, and you’re at seventy-two.

    → What Sheds It — the hourly recovery, and what’s multiplying it.
    → What Would Start It — the energy floor, and how far you are from it.
    → The Night Ahead — what sleeping now would take off.

"running on empty" is itself an `<Open>` to the energy dial. Two ways in inside one spoken clause. No coefficient table; the 0.35 an hour it sheds and the 1.6 an hour it gains below fifteen energy are in the sentences, and the last line of the body says so once in `.hint`.

**Depth 3 — `flow:person_000001/stress-recovery`, in place under that paragraph.** `parent` is the dial, so it expands rather than opening a pane. `recovery = modifierFor(person, 'recoveryRate') × personalityOf(person, 'stressRecovery')`, written as two named halves and the traits actually contributing.

    What Sheds It
    You shed stress faster than most people do.
    → Highly Strung — nothing much gets under your skin, and it costs you.
    → Sleeps Anywhere — you go out like a light, wherever you are.
    → Steadiness — you sit well above the middle of that scale.

    SLATE holds every craft trait for you, and the prodigy rule refuses
    to subtract: four traits that would have cost you here were discarded.

That last line is `provenance`. It is the `favourableOnly` asymmetry at attributes.ts:1345 stated honestly, in one line, at the foot of a body — not a level, not a panel, not openable.

**Depth 4 — `trait:person_000001/highly_strung`, in the pane.** `parent` is the flow, but the trait is a different object, so this one crosses and the pane opens with the full trail. The body is the trait's own `description` and its written `cost` string, both of which have only ever appeared on the character-creation screen, plus every knob it moves — each of which is a way back into a dial.

**Depth 5 — `dial:person_000001/sleep-quality`, and the fold.** Highly Strung moves sleep quality, so pressing it opens a fifth level: `You › How You Are › Stress › Highly Strung › Sleep Quality`. Sleep quality is the largest single lever on the energy the player sees and is displayed nowhere, so this is a real destination, not a manufactured one. From here, the trait that got you here is one of its own drivers — press it and the path folds back to depth 4 rather than growing to six, because `open()` pops to a subject already in the path.

Getting out at any depth: press any crumb, press the word you opened (for an in-place level it is still on screen, unmoved), or Escape once per level. Depth 5 costs what depth 2 costs.

What had to be written for all five: about a dozen sentences. Every figure was already there.
guards: `tests/looks.test.ts` — every door opens onto something, extended from routes to things. Boots a fresh save through `bootstrap`, then for every kind in `lookKinds()` resolves the seed subjects and follows `ways[].to` transitively to fixed point, asserting each edge resolves and no way points at an unregistered kind. This is the same guarantee, in the same shape, as `tests/navigation.test.ts`, whose own header records that this class of bug has already shipped twice.

The name gate, in the same file — for every `Looked` reached by the crawl, `name` and `kind` must fail `/_|\/|\d{4}/` and must not contain the text of any registered kind. 'Sleep Debt' passes. 'sleepDebt', 'Atlantic/Reykjavik', 'person_000001' and 'Dial' cannot ship. Two more assertions beside it: `summary` is non-empty, starts with a capital, ends in a full stop or a question mark, and contains no exclamation mark; `gone` is present on every registered view.

The shape gate, in the same file — a body whose rendered output contains more than one `.stat-grid`, or a `Stat` grid with no sentence above it, fails. This is the only defence against a look becoming a record view, and it is the rule most likely to be broken by a contributor in a hurry.

The static scan, appended to `tests/navigation.test.ts` — reads every file under `src/ui/`, matches `at('<kind>'` and `look={at('<kind>'` literals, and asserts each names a registered kind. Catches the typo the runtime crawl cannot reach, and it fails at the moment somebody writes the bad line rather than when somebody clicks it.

The affordance gate, appended to `tests/interface.test.ts` — no `title=` attribute anywhere in `src/ui/**` outside the weather-emoji allowlist; no `cursor: pointer` in `app.css` on a selector that is not rendered as a `button`; no rendered control whose whole text is Open, Show, Hide, Details, More, View, Expand, OK, Submit, Go or Continue. Two of those ship on Home today (Home.tsx:159, :188), which is the point.

`tools/label-sweep.mjs` extended from `src/engine/**/*.ts` to `src/ui/looks/**` — `name`, `kind`, `Way.label`, `Facet.label` and `Act.label` are labels and are Title Case, every word. `--write` re-cases the plain ones.

`tools/voice-check.mjs` extended to `src/ui/looks/**` — `summary`, `gone`, `Way.detail`, `Act.consequence` and `provenance` are prose and contract the way speech does. Every new sentence in the feature lives in one directory, so this is the difference between policed prose and a hundred unpoliced strings.

`tools/text-caps.mjs` — iterates `lookKinds()`, opens each at `/look?look=<kind>:<seed id>`, and measures at its existing five widths. Nothing clipped, crushed or bleeding, in the pane at 560px and full width. Enumerability is what makes this possible: a layer no tool can open is a layer no tool can see, which is how every hand-wired drill in this repo's history rotted.

`tools/ui-audit.mjs` — the same enumeration at four widths, plus one assertion the survey earns: at every width, an element carrying `.link` inside a look has a resolvable subject, and no element outside a look paints a pointer cursor.

`tools/cohesion-walk.mjs` — opens a look, navigates to the Calendar, comes back, and asserts the rail still marks the right screen. That probe (`.rail [aria-current="page"]`) is exactly what a `?look=` on the route breaks if `screenRoute()` is missed at any comparison site, and the walk already fails on 'a rail that marks the wrong screen' by name.
`tools/inventory.mjs --check` — every registered kind has a line in `docs/COVERAGE-MATRIX.md`, alongside every command and route. A kind with no matrix line is a layer nobody signed off.

`tests/monte-carlo.test.ts` — for each random life it plays, resolve every kind against that save. Catches the view that throws on a household with no members, an account with no postings, or a day in the polar night, none of which a fresh save contains.
firstSteps: 1. Portal `Modal` to a single root-level layer host and move Escape ownership to one capture-phase `window` listener that also swallows bare `h`/`c` while anything is open. Independent of the feature, fixes a live bug (the three TimeControls dialogs render at z-index 20 under `.topbar` and therefore beneath the mobile rail drawer at 30), and is the one repair nothing else will ever motivate.

2. Write `src/ui/looks/subject.ts` and `registry.ts` — `Subject`, `defineLook`, `resolveLook`, `lookExists`, `lookKinds`, `trailTo`, `subjectForRef`, `screenRoute`. No components, no CSS, no screens touched. Pure functions with a `Simulation` argument, which is what makes step 3 possible before there is anything to look at.

3. Write `tests/looks.test.ts` — the crawl, the name gate, the required `summary`/`gone` — while there are two views, not forty. Make `labelForRoute` throw on a look-bearing route in the same commit. The guard exists before the surface, or it never catches up to it.

4. Build the three containers and `<Open>`: in-place expansion (`.look-body`, two surface steps), the 560px pane, and the `/look` route for `dwell`. Wire `screenRoute()` through every existing `route ===` comparison — GameShell, WorkspaceRouter, the rail's `aria-current`, `navigate`'s dedupe — and add the trail rendering, fed by `trailTo`.

5. Add `look?: Subject` to `Stat` and `Meter`. Delete `Meter.hint`, delete `Term`, delete `.tooltip-term`, delete `.cal-event { cursor: pointer }`. This is eighteen lines and it is what makes roughly forty numbers on Home openable without restructuring a screen.

6. Build the Stress chain end to end — person, wellbeing facet, dial, flow, trait — because it is five real layers, six of its nine dials are pure exposure, and it is the case that proves prose-first. Do not build a second chain until this one reads as a life rather than a sheet.

7. Sweep the two screens that exist. Delete `CalendarWorkspace`'s local `detail` state and open `at('entry', id)` from both lists and from Home, so the same entry opens the same way in three places. Replace `DecisionItem.route` and `Notification.route` at their call sites with `subjectForRef`, so an Open button names its subject instead of a room.

8. Extend `label-sweep.mjs` and `voice-check.mjs` to `src/ui/looks/**`, teach `text-caps.mjs` and `ui-audit.mjs` to enumerate `lookKinds()`, add the kinds to `docs/COVERAGE-MATRIX.md`, and add the resolve-every-kind pass to the monte-carlo run. Ship this in the same release as step 6, not after it.

9. Only then, the breadth: the place chain, the money chain, the day chain, the estate. Each is one file in `src/ui/looks/`, each is a reviewable diff, and each is opened and measured by the tools the moment it is registered.

designs.name: The Trail — one address per level, carried in the route
designs.oneLine: Every drillable thing gets a string address; the drill stack is that address list carried inside the existing `route` string, so `navigate` pushes, `back` pops, and the breadcrumb trail the shell already renders becomes the depth stack the game does not have.
designs.mechanism:
THE ADDRESS. A segment is `kind:key` (first colon splits; key may be empty). A path is segments joined by `/`. Examples: `person:person_000001/wellbeing/dial:stress`, `city:is-39-reykjavik/tax:income`, `acct:acct_000003/txn:txn_000005`. `kind:key` is deliberately the exact shape of `{refType, refId}`, which already sits on `CalendarEntry` (calendar.ts:57-58), `DecisionItem`, `Notification`, `ScheduledItem` and `LedgerTransaction`, and as `{type,id}` pairs in `HistoryRecord.refs` — so `addressOfRef(entry)` is one line and five record types become openable at once.

WHERE IT LIVES. Not a second state tree beside the router — inside it. `route` becomes `/home?look=person:person_000001/wellbeing/dial:stress`. `tests/navigation.test.ts:74` already does `route.split('?')[0]`; query strings are anticipated by the existing guard and produced by nothing. This is the whole argument for the angle: `game-context.tsx:161-180` already implements push-with-truncate (`navigate` finds an existing crumb by route and slices back to it) and pop (`back`). Putting the path in the route means `back()` *is* pop-one-level, a crumb click *is* jump-to-ancestor, `recent`/`favourites` serialise a drill for free, and the hotkeys at :268-279 that currently change the screen underneath an open modal now correctly take the drill with them. No new stack, no focus trap, no portal, no Escape ownership fight.

THE REGISTRY. `defineLens`, modelled on the deleted `defineScene` — the precedent sweep's own verdict that scenes.ts is the closest thing SLATE ever had to this. A lens declares `kind`, `scope` ('root' or 'nested', never both), `resolve(sim, key, parent)`, `title` (the world's name — becomes the crumb), `eyebrow`, `gone` (what to say when the address resolves to nothing, in the world's voice), `render`, and optional `children()` returning addresses.

RESOLUTION. `resolvePath` walks segments left to right. For each, it asks the parent lens's registered nested kinds first; if none matches, it falls back to the root registry. So the path is a **trail, not a containment tree**: `.../dial:stress/trait:highly-strung` crosses from a field of a person into a separate object, and the trail records the walk honestly. This kills the stale-snapshot class outright — every level re-resolves from `sim` on every render, the way `useWorld` already does, so an entry that goes `missed` under an open level says so (CalendarWorkspace.tsx:27 currently freezes a `CalendarEntry` projection while the clock runs at a world minute per real second).

RENDERING. Not modals. `.side-by-side` (app.css, minmax(240px,1fr) + a 220-320px sidebar, collapsing at 700px) is fully written and used nowhere. `<LookRail/>` mounts once in `GameShell` inside `.main-inner` and renders the tip of the trail beside the screen, full-width sheet below 700px. The screen you drilled from stays on the page. This sidesteps all four Modal defects the primitives sweep found (shared window Escape, double-dimmed backdrop at 3.2% visibility, no focus restore, `title: string`) without touching Modal.

ONE BUG THIS INTRODUCES AND MUST FIX IN THE SAME COMMIT. `GameShell.tsx:190` (`route === '/home'`, `route.startsWith('/workspace/')`), `WorkspaceRouter.tsx:8` (`WORKSPACES[route]`) and the rail's `aria-current={route === item.route}` all compare the raw route. Drilled from the calendar, `/workspace/calendar?look=…` hits `startsWith` then misses the map and renders "Nothing Here Yet"; the rail stops marking the current screen, which `tools/cohesion-walk.mjs` fails on by name. Fix is one exported `screenRoute(route)` used in all three places.
designs.immersion:
The `kind` never reaches the screen. A lens has `kind` and `title` as separate fields, which is STYLE.md's label-map rule (`PERFORMER_NOUN`, `DISCIPLINE_LABEL`) made structural: `title()` returns "You", "How You Are", "Stress" while the address says `person`/`wellbeing`/`dial:stress`. There is no code path by which a type name becomes a heading — the failure mode where a modal ends up titled "Shootday" is not reachable.

The parent stays on screen. A side rail rather than a modal means drilling never blanks the thing you drilled from. Two stacked `--overlay` backdrops leave the parent 3.2% visible; that is the literal opposite of looking closer.

Every lens leads with a sentence. Render contract: prose first, facts second, ways on third. `wellbeingSummary` (life.ts:96-105) is the existing proof this reads as a life rather than a record — seven floats collapsed into "Badly short on sleep. Everything is harder than it should be."

There is no "How This Was Calculated" lens, and there must never be one. A factor renders as a **thing you have** that opens — a personality trait, an axis of how you are, last night's sleep — not as a term in a product. The floor of a trail is a person, a place, an object or a moment; the moment it is a formula, the bottom of every drill is the engine. This is the one rule I would enforce by review rather than by test.

`gone` is required on every lens. A dead address says something in the world's voice, not "That workspace doesn't exist" (WorkspaceRouter.tsx:14) or `'No such decision.'` (world.ts:37). And a lens must exist for a `kind` before any `open` prop can name it, so the Locked-toast anti-pattern (GameShell.tsx:46-49) has nowhere to attach.

No new glyphs. The rail's close control reads "Back To How You Are", built from the parent lens's `title()`. `‹ › ✦ ✕ ▾` do not multiply, because the only new affordances are a hover state on `.stat-open`/`.meter-open` and the breadcrumb `›` that already ships.
designs.depth:
The trail is always the whole path, screen included, and it is already rendered (GameShell.tsx:155-169). One gesture at every level: press a crumb to go back to it, `back()` to pop one. Depth 5 costs exactly what depth 2 costs — this is the direct answer to InstagramApp, where five independent nullable states meant 32 combinations and `openWho` closed the post to open the profile, so Back skipped a level. One array has one state.

The trail is derived from the address, not from click history. Pressing the Stress meter on Home is one click that lands at depth 3 with a full trail — `Home › You › How You Are › Stress` — because the intermediate crumbs are materialised by `resolvePath` walking the segments. A notification carrying `refType/refId` deep-links the same way and the player is never at depth 4 with one crumb and no idea where they are.

Two changes to the existing crumb code. `.slice(-6)` (game-context.tsx:167) becomes 12 with the *middle* elided rather than the head dropped, so Home never falls off. And `recent` (line 169) filters look-bearing routes, or "recently visited" fills with five levels of one drill.

Lateral moves stay lateral. `.tabs`/`.tab` is fully styled in app.css:749-762 and used nowhere; facets of one object (a person's Craft / Standing / Money / History) are tabs *inside* a level, not four more levels. Depth then counts only real containment or a real crossing to another object, which is what keeps a 5-deep trail readable as a sentence.

Crossing is honest. `.../dial:stress/trait:highly-strung` is a real walk from a number to a thing about you, and the crumb reads that way. Because resolution is relative-then-absolute, the same trait lens serves being reached from a dial, from the character sheet, or from a decision's prose — one lens, many doors, which is what CalendarWorkspace already gets right by opening the same `EntryDetail` from two lists.

Home.tsx today (line 201) renders `<Meter label="Stress" value={player.wellbeing.stress} invert />` — inert, because `Meter` renders a div. One prop:

```tsx
<Meter label="Stress" value={player.wellbeing.stress} invert
       open={`person:${player.id}/wellbeing/dial:stress`} />
```

Route becomes `/home?look=person:person_000001/wellbeing/dial:stress`. Crumbs: `Home › You › How You Are › Stress`.

L1 — `person:person_000001`
```tsx
defineLens<Person>({
  kind: 'person', scope: 'root',
  resolve: (sim, id) => sim.universe.people[id],
  title: (sim, p) => (p.id === sim.player.id ? 'You' : p.displayName),
  eyebrow: (_s, p) => PERFORMER_NOUN[p.performerTitle],
  gone: 'Nobody by that name is in this life.',
  children: (_s, p) => [`person:${p.id}/wellbeing`, `person:${p.id}/standing`, `person:${p.id}/craft`],
  render: ({ subject }) => <PersonLens person={subject} />,
});
```
Opens with a sentence about who you are, then three ways on. This is also the front door for the rail's `.rail-you` block (GameShell.tsx:141-149), which is the player's own name rendered as a plain div.

L2 — `wellbeing`
```tsx
defineLens<Person>({
  kind: 'wellbeing', scope: 'nested',
  resolve: (_sim, _key, parent) => parent as Person,
  title: () => 'How You Are',
  gone: 'There is nobody here to ask after.',
  children: (_s, p) => WELLBEING_DIALS.map((d) => `person:${p.id}/wellbeing/dial:${d.key}`),
  render: ({ subject }) => <WellbeingLens person={subject} />,

```

Six of those are simulated every day and appear on no screen in the game today. Depth here is exposure, not invention: the panel is `player.wellbeing` rendered.

L3 — `dial:stress`
```tsx
defineLens<{ person: Person; dial: WellbeingDial }>({
  kind: 'dial', scope: 'nested',
  resolve: (_sim, key, parent) => {
    const dial = WELLBEING_DIALS.find((d) => d.key === key);
    return dial ? { person: parent as Person, dial } : undefined;

  title: (_s, { dial }) => dial.label,          // 'Stress'
  gone: 'That is not one of the ways a person can be.',

```
`DialLens` for stress renders a sentence — "Eighteen, and it has been low. Nothing has asked much of you yet." — then the ways it moves, each named as a **thing**, not a term: it only starts climbing once you drop under fifteen energy; it sheds a little every hour you are not under it; a night's sleep takes a chunk off. Then the drivers as `Row`s with addresses: `trait:highly-strung`, `axis:emotional-stability`, and `person:person_000001/wellbeing/dial:energy` — a sibling, because energy is the gate.

L4 — press **Highly Strung** → `/home?look=person:person_000001/wellbeing/dial:stress/trait:highly-strung`, crumbs `Home › You › How You Are › Stress › Highly Strung`. The trait lens shows what it is, that it is one of the four you chose at creation, its written `cost` string (which today appears only on the creation screen), and the other knobs it touches — each of which opens. `back()` pops exactly one level, with no code written for it: it is `game-context.tsx:172-180` unchanged.
designs.costs:
**Addresses are stringly-typed.** `dial:stres` is a runtime miss, not a compile error. Mitigated by per-lens address builders and by extending `tests/navigation.test.ts` — which already reads sources statically rather than walking the app — from "every route opens onto a screen" to "every `open=` literal in src/ui names a registered lens kind". The raw-string escape hatch will still get used at 2am.

**Relative-then-absolute resolution is clever, and clever rots.** A kind that is both a valid child of X and a valid root would resolve differently depending on where you stand. The `scope: 'root' | 'nested'` field exists only to forbid that, and needs a test asserting no kind is registered twice. If that discipline slips, the same address means two things.

**Dead addresses are the new dead routes, at a hundred times the surface.** The navigation test's own header says this has gone wrong twice already, with two routes. Now every noun in prose is a candidate. A registered lens guarantees a *renderer*, not a *subject* — a stale `refId` still resolves to nothing, and every lens needs a `gone` sentence written by hand, in voice. That per-lens writing is the real, unglamorous cost of the whole feature, and it does not shrink with cleverness.

**It does not fix Modal, and someone will want it to.** The three TimeControls dialogs stay modals, still trapped under `.topbar`'s `z-index: 20` (app.css:585-588) and still rendering beneath the mobile rail drawer. Opening a lens from inside the Sleep dialog closes the dialog and loses its state. That is genuinely bad, and it is the sharpest thing I am foreclosing: this engine is for reading the world, not for committing to it. The precedent sweep's line is the right boundary — a scene is a drill-down that commits, a drill-down is a scene that only reads — and dialogs stay on the scene side.

**A side rail is weaker than anchored reveal-in-place.** Pressing the Stress meter opens a panel to the right, not underneath the meter. I am trading a little "looking closer" fidelity for one unbounded stack. A lens could later declare `inline: true` for depth-1, but lenses rendering in two places doubles the layout surface and `tools/text-caps.mjs` measures at five widths.

**Route strings get long and are now load-bearing.** `/home?look=person:person_000001/wellbeing/dial:stress/trait:highly-strung` never faces the player, but it faces `recent`, `favourites` (localStorage, so an old favourite can point at a lens that no longer exists), and every `route ===` comparison in the shell. Three of those comparisons are wrong the moment this ships and must be fixed in the same commit.

**I would not persist it into the save.** The path is one string, so persistence is now trivially possible — and it is the wrong call. The world moves while you are away; resuming a save four levels inside a number you were looking at last Tuesday is stranger than landing on Home.

designs.name: The Long Look
designs.oneLine: One persistent column to the right of every screen that always holds exactly one subject, addressed as `{type, id}` and re-resolved from `sim` on every tick, where depth is a named trail plus lateral facet tabs rather than a stack of covering panes.
designs.mechanism:
The shell grows a third column. `.shell-body` is already `display:flex` with `.rail` (232px, fixed) + `.main` (flex:1) at `src/styles/app.css:651`; the inspector is a fourth sibling at 360px with `border-left: 1px solid var(--line)` and its own `overflow-y:auto`. It never covers `.main`. Nothing is portalled, no z-index is claimed, and `.topbar`'s stacking context (app.css:585, the thing that already traps the three TimeControls dialogs) is irrelevant because there is no overlay.

Three parts.

1. THE ADDRESS. `Subject = { type: string; id: string }`. `id` is opaque to the inspector and interpreted only by that type's registered view, so compound addresses cost nothing: `{type:'dial', id:'person_000001/stress'}`, `{type:'attribute', id:'person_000001/breath_control'}`, `{type:'day', id:'2026-09-10'}`. That matters because the survey's central finding is that the depth lives in sub-objects with no ids — Wellbeing, Reputation, Posting, AuditFactor, Recurrence, DecisionItem.actions. An engine keyed on top-level record ids would miss almost all of it. It also means `subjectForRef(refType, refId)` is a five-line function that finally reads `CalendarEntry.refType/refId` (calendar.ts:57-58), `DecisionItem.refType/refId` (model.ts:784), `Notification` (model.ts:797), `LedgerTransaction` and `HistoryRecord.refs[]` — five declarations of one shape, one resolver.

2. THE REGISTRY. `defineSubject(type, view)` at module load, deliberately modelled on the deleted `defineScene` — a declared graph, not per-screen wiring, so `tools/walkthrough.mjs` can open every layer without hardcoding a click on the literal text "NBCUniversal", `tools/ui-audit.mjs` can measure every layer at four widths, and a test can assert every declared way resolves. A view has two halves: `resolve(sim, id)` returns the live subject or `undefined`, and `render(subject, ctx)` returns a `Resolved` — `{ name, kind, summary, facets?, body?, ways?, acts?, provenance? }`. `name` is the world's own name and is the only thing the trail ever prints, which structurally kills the "Home › Is 39 Reykjavik" hazard in `labelForRoute` (game-context.tsx:308-312): a call site cannot forget to pass a label because call sites do not pass labels.

3. THE AFFORDANCE. `<Open to={subject}>` is the single way to re-point the inspector, and it refuses to lie: it calls `useWorld(s => subjectExists(s, to))` and renders its children as plain text when nothing resolves. That is the calendar-pill bug (`.cal-event` paints `cursor:pointer` on spans with no handler, app.css:791) made structurally impossible, and it is the honest answer to the Locked-toast anti-pattern (GameShell.tsx:46) — a drill that would end in "Under Construction" simply is not painted as a drill. `Stat` and `Meter` each gain one optional `open?: Subject` prop, which is the cheapest lever in the codebase: roughly twenty Stats and seven Meters on Home light up in a single edit to `primitives.tsx`.

LIVENESS. The inspector stores addresses, never objects. `Inspector.tsx` does `const view = useWorld(s => resolveSubject(s, top))` — so it re-derives on every version bump, i.e. every world minute. This kills outright the class of bug that froze `EntryDetail` (CalendarWorkspace.tsx:27 captures a `CalendarEntry`, which `toEntry` rebuilds on every read, while the clock runs at one world minute per real second underneath it). VehiclesWorkspace was the only precedent that passed an id; this makes passing an id the only option.

ESCAPE AND STATE. `{ trail: Subject[]; facet?: string }` lives beside `route`/`breadcrumbs` in `game-context.tsx` and persists to `localStorage` per save id, the way `favourites` already does (game-context.tsx:290-300) — no schema migration, and a reload comes back looking at what you were looking at. Because the inspector is not a dialog, there is exactly one Escape owner in the app: Escape pops one level of the trail; at depth 1 it does nothing. The global `h`/`c` hotkeys (game-context.tsx:268-279) get one added guard — they navigate `.main` and leave the inspector pointed where it is, which is correct: you can walk to the Calendar while still holding your own Stress open.

THE DIVISION OF LABOUR. Modals ask, the inspector tells. `Modal` stays exactly as written for the three commit dialogs (Sleep, Skip, Advance confirm) because those are questions with consequences. Nothing read-only opens a modal ever again; `CalendarWorkspace`'s local `detail` state is deleted and both call sites (:147, :177) become `open({type:'entry', id: entry.id})`. `Meter`'s vestigial `hint` prop is deleted in the same pass, so there are never two answers to "what is behind this number".

THE WIDE ESCAPE HATCH. Because a view returns data rather than markup-in-a-container, the same `Resolved` can render full-width in `.main` at route `/look/:type/:id`. One renderer, two containers. That is how the 813-attribute sheet and a year-long daylight curve survive a 360px column: the inspector shows the top of them and offers one act, "Open It Full Width", which is a route change carrying the world's own name as its crumb.
designs.immersion:
Six things keep it from reading as a settings tree, and they are enforced rather than intended.

1. THE WORLD NEVER GOES DARK. This is the whole argument for the angle. A stacked modal at `--overlay: rgba(6,7,9,0.82)` applied twice leaves the parent 3.2% visible and three times leaves it 0.6% — drilling in makes the thing you drilled from disappear, which is the precise opposite of looking closer. The inspector takes a column and covers nothing. Home stays fully lit while you read your own Stress. The clock in the top bar keeps running, in view, one metre from the number you are examining.

2. NAMES ARE THE WORLD'S, BY CONSTRUCTION. `Resolved.name` and `Resolved.kind` come from the view, and the trail prints nothing else. No slug is ever prettified, no route segment is ever title-cased, no `refType` reaches a heading. A test walks the registry and fails any `name` or `kind` containing `_`, `/`, a digit-run of four or more, or any of the type ids themselves — so 'Sleep Debt' passes and 'sleepDebt', 'Atlantic/Reykjavik' and 'Shootday' cannot ship. `kind` is deliberately not the type: the eyebrow above Stress reads "How You Are", not "Dial".

3. PROSE FIRST, AND `summary` IS REQUIRED. Every level opens with a sentence in the character's frame before any number. `wellbeingSummary` (life.ts:96-105) is already the correct shape and is the model: it turns seven floats into "Badly short on sleep. Everything is harder than it should be." A view that has only numbers to offer has to write the sentence anyway, which is the pressure that keeps a layer from being a record dump.

4. NO SECOND STAT GRID. The failure mode of the naive version is that drilling nine Stats produces eighteen Stats. The inspector's body has three shapes and a Stat grid is not the default: a ranked list of sentences (`.list-item` rows, the one primitive already shaped for "a list of objects"), a single figure with its sentence, or a facet. Numbers appear inside sentences — "you shed about 0.35 a hour, and Highly Strung is taking a tenth off that" — not in label/value cells.

5. NO GLYPHS, NO TOOLTIPS. A way in is a named row: the label plus a `detail` line, which is exactly the `.menu-item` two-line shape TimeControls already ships and the only genuinely good affordance in the build. No chevrons, no ▾, no ✦, nothing for `title=` to hide in. The nine existing `title=` tooltips are the map of where a layer was wanted and a tooltip was written instead, and each becomes a way or a summary. `Term` gets deleted rather than fixed.

6. THE FLOOR IS ALWAYS A THING, NEVER A FORMULA. `provenance` is a single footnote line at the bottom of a level — "SLATE's calibration, derived from Iceland's price band and the city's population, not looked up" — and is never itself a subject you can open. There is no "How This Was Calculated" level anywhere, because the moment one exists the bottom of every drill is the engine. The deepest layer of any chain is a person, a place, a thing or a moment. Where a chain genuinely bottoms out, the level says so in a sentence — "That's all there is to this one." — rather than manufacturing a level, and `ways: []` renders that automatically.

The one immersion risk I cannot design away is that a permanent panel is a permanent piece of furniture. It is a place in the interface, and it is on screen when you did not ask for it. Mitigation: it is empty by default and holds a single line — "Press anything to look at it closer." — rather than a menu, and it collapses to a 40px spine you can reopen. But an empty column is a weaker opening state than nothing at all.
designs.depth:
One panel has one real hazard: at layer 4 the player has forgotten layer 2 and there is nothing on screen to remind them, because nothing is behind anything. Five devices, in order of how much work they do.

1. THE TRAIL, FULLY RENDERED AND WORLD-NAMED. Along the top of the inspector: `Yourself › How You Are › Stress › What Sheds It`. Every crumb is a button that truncates the trail to it. Unlike the shell's breadcrumbs it is not capped at six (`.slice(-6)`, game-context.tsx:167) and does not dedupe by route, which is the bug that would collapse two different people in the same workspace into one crumb. Past five levels the middle collapses to a single "…" that expands. This is the map and the back button at once, and it is the reason depth is legible without being spatial.

2. THE PARENT LINE. Above the name, in dim text: the immediate parent's name and its one-line summary. Each level cites the one above it, so layer 4 always shows layer 3's sentence. That is the single cheapest replacement for the context a stack gets from the pane behind it, and it is better than a stack's, because a stack shows you the parent's edges rather than its point.

3. FACET TABS — THE ANTI-CORRIDOR DEVICE, and the most important one. Once a subject is open, its aspects are tabs inside that level, not four more levels. A person is not Person › Wellbeing › Stress and Person › Money and Person › Standing as three descents; it is one level with tabs — How You Are, Standing, The Work, Where You've Been — using the `.tabs`/`.tab` CSS already fully written at app.css:749-762 and rendered nowhere. This is what stops the graph from being a corridor: the rule is that a tab is a facet of the same thing, a way is a different thing. Applied properly, most of the survey's "[4 layers]" and "[5 layers]" targets are two or three levels of subject and a row of tabs, and the trail stays short.

4. WAYS CARRY THEIR CONSEQUENCE. No blind descent: every way is a label plus a line saying what is behind it, so you can read the graph without walking it. "What Sheds It — the hourly recovery, and the four traits multiplying it." That is TimeControls' `.menu-item-label` + `.menu-item-detail` shape, which the repo already proved reads well.

5. FLOORS THAT ANNOUNCE THEMSELVES. `ways: []` renders a closing sentence, so no level ends in silence and no level ends in a toast. And because `Open` refuses to paint when a subject does not resolve, the player never presses something that goes nowhere. The seventeen declared-but-unstored types (Bill, StudioPlant, Structure, Room, Costume, Company…) are a live trap for any router that walks model type names; here they simply have no registered view, so they cannot be addressed, and the wide/full-width variant of the same view is where a genuinely large leaf goes.

What this does not solve: it is a corridor for the player who genuinely wants layer 5 of one chain, and the only thing carrying them is a text trail. A stack at least gives a physical sense of how far in you are. I think the trail plus the parent line is enough for four; at five and beyond the honest answer is that the facet rule should have collapsed some of those levels, and if it did not, the design is wrong at that subject rather than at the engine.

designs.costs:
WHAT IT MAKES HARDER

1. Phones, and this is the real weakness. There is no room for a persistent column below about 1024px. It has to become a bottom sheet at 65% height, which is a modal wearing a different name — the "the world never goes black" argument, which is the entire case for this angle, degrades to "the top third of the world stays visible". The rail already solves the same problem by folding into a drawer at 900px (app.css:632), so the pattern exists, but I should not pretend the angle survives intact at 400px. Every competing angle beats this one on a phone.

2. You cannot hold two objects at once. Ever. No comparing this account against that one, no showing an entry beside the entry it clashes with — and the Clash chip is the most interesting drill in the build precisely because `entriesBetween` (calendar.ts:110-121) knows the pairing. The best I can do is cite the other side in the summary with a way into it, which turns a comparison into two sequential looks. A master-detail split does this properly and this does not.

3. Space taken from `.main` at every desktop width. 232px rail + 360px inspector = 592px of chrome; `.main-inner`'s 1180px max-width has to drop to about 940, and Home's `grid-3` rows will want to become `grid-2`. That is a real re-layout of the only two screens that exist, and it is a permanent tax paid whether or not the inspector is being used. Making it collapsible softens the tax and softens the word "persistent" — a collapsed inspector means clicking a Stat has to spring it open, which is a state change the player did not ask for.

4. A narrow column is a hard ceiling on what a layer can be. A year-long daylight curve at 64°N, an hourly temperature curve, six accounts of postings, an 813-attribute sheet: none of these fit 360px. The `/look/:type/:id` full-width route is the escape hatch and it is honest — same registered view, wider container — but it means the angle needs a second container after all, and every view author has to think about both.

5. One view per subject type, and the survey implies roughly forty of them before the graph feels complete. That is the bulk of the work and it is not clever work. It is additive and each one is testable in isolation, which is the mitigation, but nobody should be told this is a weekend.

6. Two containers, one rule to learn. Modals stay, for commits. A contributor under pressure will put a read-only detail in a Modal because `Modal` is right there and takes a string. The only defence is a lint rule or a test that fails a `<Modal>` with no `footer`, plus deleting `Term` and `Meter.hint` so the tempting half-measures are gone.

WHAT IT FORECLOSES

- Two drills at once, permanently. Not deferred — foreclosed by the shape.
- Per-object URLs, unless the trail is serialised into the route, which the app cannot do anyway: `react-router-dom` is a dependency imported nowhere, `route` is React state, and there is no History API in the build. The `/look/:type/:id` hatch gives one addressable level, not a path.
- A modal drill leaving a breadcrumb in the shell trail. The inspector keeps its own trail and deliberately does not push to `breadcrumbs`, because mixing "which screen am I on" with "what am I looking at" is what makes a breadcrumb read as a file path. Two trails is a cost; one merged trail was the alternative and it is worse.
- Depth that interrupts. A scene — the deleted runtime at dc03b93, which is the closest thing this repo ever had to what is being asked for — could occupy you, refuse a stale click, and resume where you left it. The inspector is read-only by construction, so anything that commits over several steps still needs the scene runtime rebuilt. `acts` handles the one-press case ("Move The Clock To It") and nothing more.

WHERE I AM LEAST SURE. That the facet-versus-way rule holds under pressure. It is the device carrying most of the anti-corridor load, it is a judgement call at every subject, and a contributor who guesses wrong turns a tidy two-level object with tabs into a five-level corridor. It cannot be enforced by a test the way the name rule can. If this angle fails in practice, that is where it will fail first.

designs.name: The Drill Stack
designs.oneLine: One portalled stack owner renders a right-anchored cascade of sheets, each level addressed as a live `{type, id}` resolved against `sim` on every render, with the ancestry printed as a pressable trail in every sheet's header so any depth is one press from any ancestor.
designs.mechanism:
FIRST, THE ANSWER TO THE ASSIGNED QUESTION: Modal cannot stack, and the stack must not be built from it. Three things I confirmed in the files rather than assumed.

(1) `primitives.tsx:126-130` registers a `window` keydown per instance. Two open Modals both close on one Escape — so does the rail drawer (`GameShell.tsx:38-43`) and the Advance menu. A chain cannot pop one level.

(2) `.topbar` at `app.css:587` is `position: relative; z-index: 20`, which establishes a stacking context. The three TimeControls dialogs render inside it, so their `.overlay` (`app.css:767`, z-index 200) is capped at 20 — under the mobile rail drawer at z-index 30 (`app.css:637`) and its shade at 29 (`app.css:694`). There is no `createPortal` anywhere in `src/`. Depth is currently decided by where in the tree you happened to press.

(3) `--overlay` is `rgba(6,7,9,0.82)`. Two stacked overlays leave the parent 3.2% visible, three leave 0.6%, and both sit at the same `padding: 10vh` with `align-items: flex-start`, so the child lands exactly on the parent. Drilling in blacks out the thing you drilled from. That is the opposite of looking closer.

So: keep `Modal` for what it is and draw a hard line — **a modal commits, a sheet only reads.** Sleep, Skip To Event and Confirm Delete stay modals because they ask a question and change the world. Everything in the 131-finding survey is reading, and reading gets sheets. `Modal` gets one fix regardless: portal it to the same layer host at z-index 400, above the stack, which also unwedges it from `.topbar`.

THE MACHINERY, in six pieces.

**A subject is `{type, id}`, never a captured object.** `type` is a registry key, not a model type name — so `'readiness'`, `'wellbeing.stress'` and `'city'` are all first-class, which is what lets the stack address a facet of a record. This matters because the survey's own finding is that the depth lives in the anonymous sub-objects (AttributeSheet, Posting, AuditFactor, Recurrence). A scheme that only addresses top-level record ids misses most of the game. It also means the engine's five existing `refType/refId` pairs (`calendar.ts:57-58`, `model.ts:784`, `:797`, `scheduler.ts:36`, `ledger.ts:98`) and `HistoryRecord.refs` are already the right shape: one `resolveRef()` makes all of them openable at once.

**A registry, not per-screen wiring.** `defineDrill({ type, resolve, name, eyebrow, body })`, modelled on `defineScene` from the deleted scene runtime. `resolve(sim, id)` re-reads the live world; `body` renders. Registration is by module side-effect from `src/ui/drill/drills/index.ts`. `everyDrill()` exports the list, which is what makes the drill graph machine-enumerable — the walkthrough can open every one, `ui-audit` can measure every one at four widths, and a test can assert every declared drill resolves against a fresh save. That is the precedent sweep's own ask, and it is the difference between this and eleven hand-wired `useState`s.

**One stack owner, one portal.** `DrillProvider` holds `DrillLevel[]`. `DrillStack` renders through `createPortal(…, document.body)` into a single layer host. `open()` always pushes and never closes anything on the way — that is the InstagramApp bug (`openWho` closed the post to open the poster, so Back skipped a level) fixed by construction. One guard: if the subject is already in the stack, `popTo` its index instead of pushing, so Parent Company → child → Parent Company folds rather than growing.

**Liveness by re-resolution.** The level holds `{type, id}`. Each render calls `resolve(sim, id)` under `useWorld`, so the world clock — one world minute per real second — updates an open sheet. This kills the frozen-snapshot class that broke both hand-rolled precedents (`CalendarWorkspace.tsx:27` captures a `CalendarEntry`, which `toEntry` rebuilds on every read). If `resolve` returns undefined the sheet stays and prints its `gone` sentence with the trail still working — a thing vanishing under the player is worse than a thing that says it is gone.

**Escape ownership, by capture.** The stack owner registers `window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey, true)`. Capture-phase on `window` fires before every bubble-phase `window` listener in the codebase, so `stopImmediatePropagation()` there is what stops one Escape from closing four sheets, the drawer and the menu together. The same listener swallows bare `h` and `c` while depth > 0 — today those still navigate the screen underneath an open dialog (`game-context.tsx:268-279` only guards INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT).

**Session persistence, not save persistence.** The stack writes to `sessionStorage` under `slate.drill` and restores on mount, dropping the whole stack if any subject fails to resolve. The scene runtime persisted into the save because a scene commits; a sheet reads, so putting "where you were looking" into `SaveUniverse` buys a `validateUniverse` surface for nothing. A refresh is the case that matters and sessionStorage covers it.

Plus: focus trapped in the top sheet, ancestors set `inert` via ref, `document.activeElement` recorded per level and restored on pop, body scroll locked while depth > 0. None of that exists on `Modal` today.

WHAT THIS BUYS ON DAY ONE. `Stat` and `Meter` take one new prop each. Roughly thirty of the survey's findings — every Stat on Home, every Stat in EntryDetail, all seven Meters — light up in eighteen lines of `primitives.tsx`, with no restructuring of `Home.tsx`. Because openability moves onto the subject, `Home.tsx:84` and `CalendarWorkspace.tsx:147` pass the same `at('entry', id)` and agree for free — which is the survey's structural finding stated as a fix.
designs.immersion:
Five rules, each answering a specific anti-pattern the sweep found on screen today.

**1. The sheet is a lens, not a window — the world stays lit.** Sheets are right-anchored at `min(560px, 100vw)`, not centred at `10vh`. Home's panels stay visible and readable down the left of a laptop. One backdrop for the whole stack at a single `--overlay`, never one per level, so depth 4 does not black out depth 0. Older sheets shift left 26px per level of remove, so you see a strip of each ancestor's edge; the strip is pressable and its accessible name is `Back To The Studio Lot`. The visual language is layered glass, not a dialog chain.

**2. The type word lives in the eyebrow, never in the title.** `Modal` takes `title: string` and nothing else, which is exactly why a caller under pressure writes "Calendar Entry" or "Property Details". `DrillDefinition` splits them: `name()` returns the world's own noun and `eyebrow()` returns the kind. So the header reads *The day* / **Tuesday The 14th**, and "Kind" as a Stat label (`CalendarWorkspace.tsx:223`) has somewhere better to go.

**3. `name()` is required and never derived.** `labelForRoute` (`game-context.tsx:308-312`) prettifies slugs when the optional label is omitted, so one forgotten argument gives you "Home › Is 39 Reykjavik". The registry makes the name a required function of the resolved value, and the gate asserts no `name()` output matches `/^[a-z]+_[0-9a-f]+$/` or contains `/`. That is the highest-leverage single fix in the whole sweep and it costs one test.

**4. No formula is ever a level.** This is where "Truth in the text" and "without breaking immersion" actually collide, and the resolution has to be structural or it will not hold. The rule: **provenance is a footnote inside a level, never a level of its own.** There is no "How This Was Calculated" drill type, and `defineDrill` is the only way to make one, so it is a reviewable line. The floor of every chain is a person, a place, a thing, a moment or an honest sentence — never an arithmetic breakdown. Readiness opens onto *which of the nine is costing you and since when*, in the register `wellbeingSummary` (`life.ts:96-105`) already writes in, not onto seven remapped multipliers. The multipliers can be the last line of that sheet, in `.hint`, once.

**5. Depth may not surface what the character cannot know.** `core/audit.ts` already has `redactForPlayer` and a `knowable` flag per factor, is fully written, and has zero callers. Any drill that wants to answer *why* terminates there rather than growing a second explanation system. That is the guarantee that keeps looking closer from becoming opening the debugger.

Two smaller things the mechanism forces: no glyphs anywhere in the chrome (the ancestor strip is a tinted column with a spoken name, the trail separator is the existing `›` already used by breadcrumbs and nothing new), and `Term` plus `.tooltip-term` get deleted along with `.cal-event { cursor: pointer }` — the nine `title=` attributes are the map of where a real layer was wanted, and each becomes an `<Open>` or goes away. Hover-only depth does not exist on a phone.
designs.depth:
The trail is the whole answer, and it lives in the sheet header rather than the shell, because the shell's breadcrumbs are behind the scrim.

`DrillTrail` reads both `breadcrumbs` from game-context and `stack` from `useDrill`, and prints one continuous path whether a step was a screen or a sheet:

    Home › How You Are › Stress › Highly Strung

The first crumb is the screen you drilled from and pressing it calls `close()`. Every middle crumb calls `popTo(i)`. So **any depth is one press from any ancestor** — depth 5 costs the same as depth 2, which is the thing five independent nullable booleans in InstagramApp could never do.

Four ways out, in the order a player finds them:

1. **The trail.** One press to any ancestor or all the way out. Primary, always visible, worded.
2. **The ancestor's visible edge.** The 26px strip to the left of the top sheet is a button that pops to that level. This is the gesture the cascade exists to make available — you can see the thing you came from, so you can press it.
3. **Escape.** Pops exactly one level, owned at capture phase so nothing else fires.
4. **The backdrop.** Closes the whole stack. Pressing the world means going back to the world; making it pop one level would be a slower version of Escape with no way to say "all the way out".

Deliberately not bound: Backspace. It fights the browser and text fields for no gain the trail does not already give.

Beyond depth 3 the DOM stays bounded — only the top three sheets render, deeper ancestors exist as trail crumbs only, and the trail elides its middle once it passes five: `Home › The Estate › … › Stage Two › The Rig`. The elision is a button that opens the full path as a list.

The rule that keeps depth from being noise: **narrowing a set is a filter inside one level, not a new level.** Choosing among the 813 attributes uses the `.picker-results` shape (already built in `LocationPicker`, wrongly stranded in `src/ui/creation`) inside the sheet you are already in. A new level means you are looking at a *different object*. Without that rule the stack grows a level per list click and the trail turns into a click log — which is the failure mode this angle is most exposed to.

And `navigate()` closes the stack. A sheet floating over a screen it does not belong to is worse than losing your place.
designs.costs:
**Where the angle is genuinely weak.**

*The cascade's whole argument dies on a phone.* Below 700px sheets go full width, the offsets go to zero, and the ancestor strips disappear — so on the device where context matters most, drilling covers the world exactly the way a modal does, and the trail is doing all the work alone. I would not claim otherwise. It means the trail's wording has to be right, not decorative, and it means a 26px strip is a laptop affordance the design cannot lean on.

*It forecloses reveal-in-place as the default.* Four survivors independently reached for expansion rather than an overlay — the calendar's day panel, Relationships' master-detail, the three creation `<details>`, the audit `<details>` — and the honest read of that is that when the parent still matters, people do not want a layer. A right-anchored sheet is a partial answer, not the same thing. The rule I would hold: level 1 of anything that is *part of what you are already reading* stays a `<details>`/`.sheet` in place, and the stack starts when you are looking at a **different object**. That is a judgement call per call site and it will drift.

*It forecloses master-detail entirely.* `.side-by-side` is fully defined and unused, and it is the right shape for narrowing a set. The stack is the wrong shape for that, so "narrowing is a filter, not a level" has to be enforced by review. If it slips, the trail becomes a click log within a month.

*It forecloses URL-addressable depth.* I chose sessionStorage over routes because there is no URL in this app at all — react-router is a dependency imported nowhere, `route` is React state. That means a drill cannot be linked to, and the walkthrough tool gets `everyDrill()` enumeration instead of addresses it can navigate to directly. Enumeration is enough to open and photograph everything, but it is not enough to say "look at this specific thing".

**What it makes harder.**

*Every drill is prose someone has to write.* The engine makes a level cheap to mount and does nothing to make it worth mounting. The survey's own best insight — that most layer 1 is exposure, not invention, because `PlaceProfile` carries 33 fields and Home prints 20 — is true and only gets you the first layer. Layers 2 and 3 are writing, and there are 131 findings.

*It makes a bad level very easy to add.* The path of least resistance in a registry is a level of Stats, and the immersion sweep is right that if drilling produces more Stats the feature has become a schema browser with good typography. `defineDrill` cannot prevent that. What it can do is make every level a reviewable diff in one directory, which is the most the machinery can honestly offer.

*Two primitives now have two shapes.* `Stat` with `open` is a button, without it a div. That is the correct affordance contract — painted clickable ⇒ opens — but it doubles the states `ui-audit` has to measure and the states CSS has to define.

*The gate does not currently see any of this.* `label-sweep` scans only `src/engine/**/*.ts` and `voice-check` only `.ts`/`.tsx`, so every string this feature adds in `src/ui/drill/` needs those tools extended, and the `.sheet` toggle words still live in a CSS `content:` string where no tool can read them. Shipping the stack under the existing gates means shipping a hundred unpoliced strings.

**What it will surface that nobody asked it to.** Depth exposes stale prose immediately. The Sleep dialog's closing paragraph (`TimeControls.tsx:143-147`) promises bills coming due and messages arriving from deleted systems; EntryDetail names an action it does not offer. The first three drills built will make both visible. That is a feature, but it is also unbudgeted work.

designs.name: Look — depth as in-place expansion, addressed by subject, declared once per kind
designs.oneLine: Every drillable thing is a `<Look subject={{kind, id}}>` whose name is the control; pressing it expands a registry-declared body in the flow of the page beneath it, nested arbitrarily deep, with the open chain held as a set of paths in GameProvider and mirrored into a sticky one-line trail so nothing ever covers anything.
designs.mechanism:
THREE PARTS, NONE OF WHICH IS A SCREEN.

1. THE ADDRESS. `LookSubject = { kind: string; id?: string }`. `kind` is a registered noun ('person', 'wellbeing.stress', 'city', 'entry', 'account', 'holiday'), `id` a world id when the subject is a record. This is deliberately the shape the engine already emits seven times and no UI reads: `CalendarEntry.refType/refId` (calendar.ts:57-58), `DecisionItem.refType/refId` (model.ts:784), `Notification` (:797), `ScheduledItem` (scheduler.ts:36), `LedgerTransaction` (ledger.ts:98), `AuditRecord.subjectType/subjectId`, `HistoryRecord.refs[]`. One resolver lights all seven at once. Subjects with no id (`wellbeing.stress`) address a field-of-the-player, which is where most of the game's depth actually lives.

2. THE REGISTRY, modelled on the deleted `defineScene`. `src/ui/looks/*.tsx` declares, once per kind, what is inside it — `name(sim, subject)`, `summary(sim, subject)`, `Body({sim, subject})`. A screen never writes a body. This is the fix for the survey's central finding: the same calendar entry is clickable in CalendarWorkspace and dead on Home because openability lives in a screen's `useState`. With a registry it lives on the kind, so the three renderings of "today" and the two of the entry agree for free.

3. THE EXPANSION. `<Look>` renders a `<button class="link">` carrying the subject's own name — the affordance the stylesheet already wrote at app.css:328 ("A name that is also a way in") and never used. Pressing it inserts the body in the document flow directly beneath, inside whatever container it already sits in. No portal, no overlay, no z-index, no focus trap, no scroll lock, nothing hidden. Escape and the same button both close it.

STATE. `LookRoot` holds `Set<string>` of open paths in GameProvider, beside `breadcrumbs`. A path is built by React context, not written by call sites: each `Look` reads the parent path off `LookPathContext` and appends `${kind}:${id ?? ''}`, so a nested Look cannot invent an inconsistent address. Because a Look only renders inside its parent's body, the set is structurally always a valid tree. Consequences that fall out for free: hoisting state to the provider means a drill survives navigate() (every deleted precedent evaporated because drill state was component-local); storing paths not objects means the body re-reads `sim` on every `version` bump, which kills the stale-snapshot bug that freezes EntryDetail against a clock running a minute a second; and the open chain is a first-class value the shell breadcrumbs can read, so the codebase's only depth machinery finally sees a drill.

SIBLINGS ARE EXCLUSIVE BY DEFAULT. Opening a Look closes any open sibling at the same path prefix. This is load-bearing, not a preference: it bounds page growth at one body per level (~4 bodies), which is the only reason depth 4 is survivable in the flow. `<LookGroup compare>` opts a container out where comparison is the point.

SCROLL, which is the whole engineering problem of this angle. `.main` is the scroller (app.css:730), not the window, so all of this is measured against `main.getBoundingClientRect()`. `LookRoot` runs one `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the open set: before React commits it records the opener row's top relative to `.main`; after commit it restores `main.scrollTop` so the opener stays at the same screen y — the thing you pressed never moves under your finger. Then, only if the new body's bottom falls below the fold, it scrolls down by `min(bodyHeight, fold - openerBottom + 24)`, instantly when `document.body.dataset.reducedMotion === 'true'` and smoothly otherwise. Closing does nothing: `overflow-anchor` is on by default and content collapsing below the anchor is correct. This is the fix for the live calendar-day bug, where a phone reveal happens off-screen and the press looks like it did nothing.

DEPTH IS NOT INDENTATION PAST LEVEL 2. Four nested 16px insets is a 64px gutter on a 360px phone. `.look-body` steps `--surface-2` then `--surface-3` and stops; every level carries a 2px left rule in `--accent-line`, and levels 3+ are flush. Depth is legible from the trail, not from the margin.

THE TRAIL. `LookRoot` renders one `position: sticky; top: 0` strip at the top of `.main-inner`, visible only when something is open: `You › How You Are › Stress`. Each crumb collapses back to that depth. It is the answer to the honest objection that at depth 3 the body is taller than the viewport and you have scrolled past what you drilled from. It is sticky, one line, 28px, and it covers nothing — it is part of the page, not over it.

WHAT STAYS A MODAL. A Look is read-only depth. Anything that commits — Sleep, Skip To Event, Delete Save — stays a Modal, because a dialog is the right shape for a decision and the wrong shape for a fact. `LookRoot`'s Escape handler no-ops while `document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]')` matches, so the two systems never fight over one key. GameProvider's `h`/`c` hotkeys gain the same guard: they currently fire behind an open dialog and change the screen underneath it.

WHAT THIS FORBIDS, ENFORCED BY CONSTRUCTION. There is no way to paint the affordance without providing a body, because `Look` renders both. A kind with no registered view throws in dev and renders as plain text in production — never a toast, never Under Construction. There is no button labelled Open, Show, Details or More anywhere in the system, because the noun is the control; STYLE.md:33-39 already forbids those words and Home ships "Open" twice today. `title=` stops being the depth mechanism: the nine tooltips in the survey become bodies. And `Term` finally has a real implementation — a word in prose that is a `Look` with a one-paragraph body.
designs.immersion:
Four properties keep it from reading as a settings tree, and each is a rule the system can hold rather than a hope.

THE NOUN IS THE CONTROL. There is no chevron, no caret, no "Details" button, no disclosure triangle. You press the word "Stress", or "Reykjavík", or "Everyday Checking", and it opens. The affordance is a dotted underline on the name — `button.link`, already in the stylesheet, already commented as "a name that is also a way in". A settings tree is made of rows with controls on them; this is made of words in sentences. It also satisfies STYLE.md:33-39 by construction, because there is never a verb to get wrong.

NOTHING IS COVERED, SO NOTHING IS LEFT. A modal chain says "you have gone somewhere". Two stacked overlays at `--overlay` leave the parent 3.2% visible — the world you drilled from goes black, which is the precise opposite of looking closer. In-place expansion keeps the summary sentence, the other two meters, and the panel's own name on screen while the detail sits underneath. You are still standing in the same place, holding the same thing, looking harder at part of it.

THE FLOOR IS NEVER A FORMULA. A `LookView.Body` may name a coefficient in a sentence but must terminate on a person, a place, an object or a moment. Readiness does not open into `energyPart × stressPart / 1.35`; it opens into "Sleep is what's costing you" and the night that caused it. Where the chain genuinely bottoms out at SLATE's own calibration, that is a footnote in the world's voice at the bottom of a body — Reykjavík's cost of living saying it's derived from Iceland's price level and the city's size — never a "How This Was Calculated" layer, because the moment one of those exists the bottom of every drill is the engine. The registry is where that rule is held: one author writes the body for a kind, once, and `tools/voice-check.mjs` and `label-sweep` (extended to `src/ui/looks/**`) see it.

THE HONEST DEAD END IS CONTENT. Reputation has never moved, because nothing writes it after `seedReputation`. Net worth's asset branch is permanently empty because the land is the family's, not the character's. Industry Presence is 0. Under this design each of those opens into the sentence that is true — "Nobody's heard of you yet. Nothing has happened to change that." — rather than a bar chart of a number that cannot move, or a toast saying Under Construction. A drill that ends in "Under Construction" breaks immersion harder than no drill; a drill that ends in a true sentence about the shape of this particular life reads better than a number would.
designs.depth:
Depth survives because four different things carry it, and none of them is indentation.

THE TRAIL CARRIES ORIENTATION. Sticky, one line, at the top of the scroller, only when something is open: `You › How You Are › Stress › Hard To Rattle`. It answers the only question deep expansion cannot answer by itself — "what am I inside?" — when the body has grown taller than the viewport and the parent's header has scrolled off. Each crumb is `collapseTo(depth)`. Because it is fed from the same open-path set, GameShell's existing breadcrumbs can concatenate it, so `Home › How You Are › Stress` is one continuous path whether a step was a route or a look. That is the depth stack for objects the codebase has never had.

EXCLUSIVE SIBLINGS BOUND THE PAGE. Without this, in-place expansion is unusable at depth 3: open six things and the page is 8,000px. With it, the page can only grow by one body per level, so a depth-4 chain adds four bodies, not fourteen. It is also how the reader keeps their place — there is exactly one open branch, so scrolling down from the trail always walks the chain in order.

SURFACE STEPS TWICE AND STOPS. `--surface-2`, then `--surface-3`, then flat, with a 2px `--accent-line` rule down the left of every body at every level. `.callout`, `.holding` and `.trait` independently landed on `--surface-2` as "one level inside a card" already; this names that convention and refuses to keep going, because a fourth tint on a dark palette is invisible and a fourth indent is 64px of gutter on a phone.

THE BODY IS A PLACE, NOT A TABLE. This is the part that actually decides whether depth 4 is worth reaching. A body is prose with Looks in it, plus at most one small group of facts. If layer 2 of a city is 18 Stats where layer 1 was 9, the drill-down is a schema browser with a nice font. So the registry ships a second content atom beside `Stat` — a `Line` of prose in which the drillable nouns are underlined — and the convention is that a body leads with a sentence and only then offers figures. Stress at depth 2 is two sentences with three underlined phrases in them, not a table of coefficients.

WHERE IT REFUSES TO GO DEEPER. A body that would be a genuine dwelling place — the whole 813-attribute sheet, the estate as a map, a full statement — is not a Look. It is a route, opened from inside a Look by a named control ("Read The Whole Sheet"). Looks are for looking; routes are for staying. Drawing that line explicitly is what stops the expansion tree from eventually containing the entire game.
